value_stream.name: Trade Show, Exhibition & Field Event Marketing

fields.Volume: Per-event booth/stand (national shows large; regional smaller)

Automation Opportunity: - Modular booth-inventory tracking; build-timeline/dependency tooling; 3D booth-preview
Controls: - CTL-648 (ensure controlled execution — Exhibition & Trade-Show Operations (PA-139.2).)
- CTL-648: booth build on timeline; brand standards met (VS-14); asset tracked
Cross-references: - links to VS-14 (brand), VS-34 (procurement/build), VS-06 (logistics), VS-87 (intl. customs), W4207 (teardown/reuse)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Late-build risk**: Booth not ready at show open; mitigated by production timeline + contingency
- **Inbound-logistics risk**: Booth/product delayed in shipping/customs; mitigated by lead-time planning (VS-06/VS-87)
System Touchpoints: - Booth-design/build procurement (VS-34); brand (VS-14); logistics (VS-06); asset tracking (modular booth)
Time Estimate: - ~4–8 weeks per flagship show build; setup 1–3 days on-site

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Designer design the booth/stand (layout, branding, product zones, demo area, meeting space, lead-capture station) aligned to brand (VS-14) and event objective (W4200)
Event Marketing/Procurement source build/fabrication, manage production timeline, and coordinate inbound logistics to the venue (shipping, customs for intl. shows, storage — links to VS-06/VS-34)
Event Marketing oversee installation/dressing at venue, resolve on-site issues, and capture build lessons for reuse (reusable modular booth inventory)

Automation Opportunity: - Contract-template library; registration automation; sponsorship-tier tracking
Controls: - CTL-648 (ensure controlled execution — Exhibition & Trade-Show Operations (PA-139.2).)
- CTL-648: show contract Legal-reviewed (VS-100.3); ABC-compliant (VS-86.3); spend reconciled (W4195)
Cross-references: - links to VS-100.3 (legal/contracts), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-34 (procurement), VS-86.3 (ABC), W4194 (priority), W4195 (budget)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Bad-location risk**: Poor booth placement reduces traffic; mitigated by early contracting/negotiation
- **Contract-risk**: Unfavorable/cancellation terms; mitigated by Legal review (VS-100.3)

steps.activity: Event Marketing negotiate/contract show space and sponsorship tier (booth location, branding rights, speaking slots, lead-list access) with the organizer, per portfolio priority (W4194)
Event Marketing manage staff/attendee registrations (badges, access, VIP passes) and coordinate with audience targeting (W4196)
Event Marketing/Legal manage the contract (payment milestones, cancellation/force-majeure, insurance, ABC — links to VS-100.3/VS-86.3), and reconcile spend (W4195)

fields.Owner: Event Marketing Manager / Merchandising (VS-01) / Trade Marketing
fields.Participants: Merchandising (VS-01), Trade Specialists (VS-124), Vendors, Logistics (VS-06), Product Info (VS-137)

Automation Opportunity: - Sample/giveaway demand planning; product-content auto-pull (VS-137); demo-checklist automation
Controls: - CTL-648 (ensure controlled execution — Exhibition & Trade-Show Operations (PA-139.2).)
- CTL-648: demo staff trained + DG safety (VS-114/VS-24); sample/giveaway inventory tracked
Cross-references: - links to VS-01 (merchandising), VS-137 (product content), VS-14 W1270 (collateral), VS-09/VS-70 (demos), VS-06 (logistics), VS-114 (DG safety), W4207 (return)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Demo-safety risk**: Live tool/chemical demo → injury; mitigated by trained staff + DG safety (VS-114/VS-24)
- **Sample-stockout risk**: Giveaways/samples run out; mitigated by demand planning + buffer
System Touchpoints: - Merchandising (VS-01); product content (VS-137); print/collateral (VS-14 W1270); logistics (VS-06); in-store services/demos (VS-09); DG safety (VS-114)

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Merchandising select display/demo products and samples/giveaways (product focus W4200), coordinate with vendors (W4197), and ensure product-content/collateral (links to VS-137 PIM, VS-14 print)
Event Marketing/Trade Specialists plan product demos (paint mixing, cutting, tool demos, solar — links to VS-09/VS-70), and train demo staff (VS-124); ensure safety for DG demos (VS-114)
Event Marketing/Logistics coordinate display/sample inbound to venue, manage inventory/giveaways on-site, and arrange post-event return/disposal (W4207)

fields.Participants: Booth staff, Trade Specialists (VS-124), Trade-Pro (VS-43), Merchandising (VS-01)
fields.Volume: Hundreds–thousands of booth visitors per show

Automation Opportunity: - Badge-scan/app lead-capture; real-time lead dashboard; AI lead-qualification scoring (governed VS-128)
Controls: - CTL-648 (ensure controlled execution — Exhibition & Trade-Show Operations (PA-139.2).)
- CTL-648: lead-capture with consent (VS-91); qualify-criteria enforced; leads routed same-day (W4214)
Cross-references: - links to VS-11/VS-107 (CRM), VS-43 (trade-pro), VS-124 (selling skills), VS-91 (consent), W4214 (lead capture), W4200 (targets)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lead-capture-failure risk**: Badges/app fail → lost leads; mitigated by reliable capture + backup
- **Engagement-quality risk**: Staff collecting cards not qualifying; mitigated by training (VS-124) and qualify-criteria
System Touchpoints: - Lead-capture system (W4214); CRM (VS-11/VS-107); trade-pro base (VS-43); consent/privacy (VS-91)
Time Estimate: - During event; booth staff per roster (W4199)

steps.activity: Booth staff engage visitors (qualify — trade-pro/contractor/developer/architect), run demos (W4203), and capture leads (scan badge/app, consent links to VS-91) into the lead-capture system (W4214)
Trade Sales/Key Accounts conduct pre-booked and walk-up meetings with named accounts/prospects (W4205), and progress opportunities (CRM links to VS-11/VS-107)
Event Lead monitor booth performance (traffic, leads, meetings vs target W4200), adjust staffing/engagement, and run daily debriefs

fields.Participants: Key Accounts (VS-107), Trade Sales (VS-11), Executives, Vendor partners, Trade-Pro (VS-43)
fields.Volume: Named accounts, key trade-pros, vendor partners, media

Automation Opportunity: - Meeting-scheduling tools; outcome-logging automation; ABC-hospitality threshold alerts
Controls: - CTL-648 (ensure controlled execution — Exhibition & Trade-Show Operations (PA-139.2).)
- CTL-648: hospitality/gifts within ABC policy (VS-86.3); meeting outcomes logged to CRM with owners
Cross-references: - links to VS-107 (key accounts), VS-11 (trade sales), VS-46 (B2G), VS-86.3 (ABC), VS-43 (trade-pro), W4214 (follow-up)
Pain Points / Risks: - **ABC risk**: Excessive hospitality/gifts to government/procurement buyers (B2G — links to VS-46); mitigated by ABC policy (VS-86.3)
- **No-follow-up risk**: Meeting outcomes not captured → lost momentum; mitigated by CRM logging + owners

steps.activity: Key Accounts/Trade Sales schedule pre-booked meetings with named accounts/key prospects (from W4196 targeting) at the booth/hospitality suite, with agendas and exec participation
Event Lead host VIPs/partners (hospitality, executive briefings, site/tour), within ABC policy for hospitality/gifts (links to VS-86.3), and capture meeting outcomes/next steps
Event Lead log meeting outcomes/commitments to CRM (VS-11/VS-107), assign follow-up owners (W4214), and ensure ABC-compliant hospitality (VS-86.3)

fields.Owner: Event Marketing Manager / Admin / Travel Coordinator
fields.Participants: HR (VS-19), Finance (VS-34.3), Travel Vendor, Event team
fields.Volume: Event-team travel (flights, hotels, per-diem) across shows

Automation Opportunity: - Travel-booking tools; expense/per-diem automation; policy-compliance checks
Controls: - CTL-648 (ensure controlled execution — Exhibition & Trade-Show Operations (PA-139.2).)
- CTL-648: travel/expense within policy (VS-34.3); receipts/reconciliation; budget tracked
Cross-references: - links to VS-34.3 (travel/expense W1686), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-19 (HR), W4195 (budget), W4216 (cost analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Policy-abuse risk**: Out-of-policy travel/expense; mitigated by policy + approval
- **Cost-overrun risk**: Travel exceeds budget; mitigated by advance booking and budget tracking
System Touchpoints: - Travel/expense policy (VS-34.3 W1686); corporate card (VS-34.3); finance (VS-17.4)
Time Estimate: - ~1 week per event travel planning + reconciliation

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Admin plan travel/accommodation (flights, hotels near venue, ground transport) for the event team, within travel policy (links to VS-34.3 W1686)
steps.r: Event Marketing Mgr / Travel Coord / Admin

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Admin/Finance manage per-diem and expense (policy-compliant, receipts, corporate-card links to VS-34.3), and brief the team on policy
Event Marketing/Finance reconcile travel expenses vs budget (W4195), manage the travel vendor, and report travel cost-efficiency (W4216)

fields.Volume: Booth/stand assets, display products, samples, collateral

workflows.name: Show Teardown, Asset Recovery & Return Logistics

Controls: - CTL-648: reusable assets tracked (VS-35); product returns reconciled (VS-05); waste disposed (VS-73)
Cross-references: - links to VS-06 (logistics), VS-05 (inventory), VS-35 (assets), VS-73 (waste), W4201 (modular booth)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Asset-loss risk**: Reusable booth/assets lost/damaged in transit; mitigated by asset tracking (VS-35) and packing discipline
- **Inventory-miscount risk**: Returned samples miscounted; mitigated by return reconciliation (VS-05)
Time Estimate: - ~1–3 days teardown + return logistics per event

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Logistics plan teardown (schedule, labor, packing, outbound shipping), and segregate reusable assets (modular booth W4201) vs consumables/disposal
steps.r: Event Marketing Mgr / Logistics / Exhibit Vendor

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Logistics return display/sample products to DC/store/inventory (links to VS-05/VS-06), and recover reusable booth assets to storage (asset tracking VS-35)
Event Marketing reconcile asset recovery (loss/damage), dispose of consumables/waste (VS-73), and capture teardown lessons

fields.Participants: HSE (VS-24), Booth staff, First-aid/medical, Venue security, LP (VS-23)
fields.Volume: Per-event HSE (crowd, demo, DG, electrical, manual handling)

workflows.name: Health, Safety & Incident Management at Events

Automation Opportunity: - HSE-risk checklist app; incident-report mobile logging; demo-safety checklists
Controls: - CTL-648 (ensure controlled execution — Exhibition & Trade-Show Operations (PA-139.2).)
- CTL-648: event HSE risk-assessed & controlled (VS-24); incidents logged/reported (VS-88); insurance where applicable (VS-26.3)
Cross-references: - links to VS-24.1/VS-24.2 (HSE/emergency), VS-114 (DG), VS-23 (security), VS-88 (records), VS-26.3 (insurance), W4203 (demo safety)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Demo/crowd-injury risk**: Live demos/crowds cause injury; mitigated by HSE controls + trained staff
- **Incident-mismanagement risk**: Poor incident response → liability; mitigated by procedure (VS-24.2) and logging
System Touchpoints: - HSE (VS-24.1/VS-24.2); DG safety (VS-114); records (VS-88); insurance (VS-26.3); LP (VS-23)
Time Estimate: - Pre-event preparedness ~1–2 days; on-site continuous; post-event reporting

steps.activity: Event Lead/HSE assess event HSE risks (crowd, live demos, DG, electrical, manual handling/assembly), and prepare controls (first-aid, fire-extinguisher, PPE, emergency contacts — links to VS-24.1)
Event Lead/Booth staff manage on-site safety (demo safety, crowd flow, DG handling VS-114), and respond to incidents (injury, illness, security) per procedure (VS-24.2)
Event Lead/HSE log/report incidents (investigation, records VS-88, insurance VS-26.3 if applicable), and capture HSE lessons for future events
